mcq.q: The true test for deciding whether a partnership exists is:
options: Sharing of profits alone
Joint ownership of property
Mutual agency — each partner acts for the others and binds them
Registration of the firm
mcq.explain: Section 6 tells courts to look at the actual relationship of the parties, judged from all the facts taken together. Sharing profits is evidence but not conclusive (Cox v. Hickman). The decisive element is mutual agency: each partner acts as agent of the others and as principal for himself.
mcq.fast: True test = mutual agency, not profit sharing.

mcq.q: The maximum number of partners in a partnership firm, as prescribed under the Companies Act, 2013 and its rules, is:
mcq.explain: Section 464 of the Companies Act, 2013 prohibits a partnership or association of more than the prescribed number of persons from carrying on business for gain unless registered as a company or formed under another law. Rule 10 of the Companies (Miscellaneous) Rules, 2014 fixes this number at 50. The old limits of 10 and 20 no longer apply.
mcq.topic: Definitions in Section 4: partnership, partner, firm, firm name
mcq.fast: Firm cap = 50 (Companies Act s.464 + Rules). 200 is the private-company cap.

mcq.q: In an HUF, the coparceners who run the family trade are:
options: Partners by birth
Not partners — partnership comes from agreement, not from birth (Section 5)
Partners if there are more than two members
Partners only if the Karta agrees
mcq.explain: Section 5 makes agreement, not status, the source of partnership. Members of an HUF carrying on a family business are not partners in respect of that business, because their rights come from birth in the family, not from an agreement.
mcq.fast: Partnership = contract. Family business by birth = status, not partnership.

mcq.q: Which of these persons becomes a partner merely by receiving a share of profits?
options: None of them — sharing profits alone does not make one a partner
A lender paid interest that varies with profits
An employee paid a bonus based on profits
The widow of a deceased partner receiving an annuity out of profits
mcq.explain: Under Section 6, receiving a share of profits or payment varying with profits does not by itself make a person a partner. A lender, a servant or agent paid by a share of profits, and the widow or child of a deceased partner receiving part of the profits are all examples given in the Act of people who are not partners on that ground alone.
mcq.fast: Profit share alone ≠ partner. Look for mutual agency.

mcq.q: A partnership in which the partners have made no provision about its duration or how it will end is:
options: A particular partnership
A partnership for a fixed term
An illegal partnership
A partnership at will — Section 7
mcq.explain: Section 7 calls a partnership "at will" where no provision is made by contract for its duration or for its determination. Such a firm can be dissolved by any partner giving written notice to all the others. A particular partnership under Section 8 is formed for a particular adventure or undertaking.
mcq.topic: Kinds of partnership and the partnership deed
mcq.fast: No duration + no ending clause = at will.

mcq.q: A person lends his name to a firm and allows himself to be represented as a partner, but has no real interest in it. He is a:
options: Sleeping partner with no liability
Sub-partner
Minor partner
Nominal partner, liable to third parties who deal with the firm on that basis
mcq.explain: A nominal partner contributes neither capital nor management and does not share profits, but lends his name to the firm. Since outsiders may deal with the firm relying on his name, he is liable to them for the firm's debts like any other partner. A sleeping partner shares profits but stays out of management.
mcq.fast: Name only, nothing else = nominal; still liable to outsiders.

mcq.q: Which statement about a partnership deed is correct?
options: A written and registered deed is compulsory
A partnership may be formed by an oral agreement; a written deed is advisable but not compulsory
A partnership without a written deed is void
Only a deed on stamp paper creates a partnership
mcq.explain: The Indian Partnership Act, 1932 does not require the partnership agreement to be in writing. A partnership may arise from an oral agreement or even from conduct. A written deed is strongly advisable because it records the terms, and registration of the firm requires a statement, but neither makes an oral partnership invalid.
mcq.topic: Kinds of partnership and the partnership deed

mcq.q: Which feature distinguishes a partnership firm from a company?
options: A firm has perpetual succession
Partners have limited liability
A firm is not a legal person separate from its partners, while a company is
A firm can have unlimited members
mcq.explain: A partnership firm is only a collective name for the partners; it has no legal personality separate from them, and partners' liability is unlimited. A company is a separate legal person with perpetual succession, and its members' liability is usually limited. A firm's membership is also capped, while a public company has no upper limit.
mcq.topic: Partnership distinguished from other forms of organisation
mcq.fast: Separate legal entity = company (and LLP), not a firm.

mcq.q: Assertion (A): Persons who jointly own a house and share the rent from it are not necessarily partners.  Reason (R): Partnership needs an agreed profit-sharing business run by all the partners, or by some acting on behalf of all.
options: A and R are both true; R explains A
A and R are both true; R does not explain A
A is true; R is false
A is false; R is true
mcq.explain: Both are true and R explains A. Co-ownership of property and sharing its income does not create a partnership, because Section 4 needs an agreed sharing of business profits, with the business run by the partners or some of them on behalf of all. Merely letting out a jointly owned house is not such a business with mutual agency.
mcq.fast: R is the definition that makes A true -> R explains A.
